ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There is a curve labeled ABC in the figure, and the question stem states that the solar altitude on this curve is 0°, namely the terminator; the vertical meridian in the figure is labeled 180°, and point B is located above this meridian and close to the northernmost position of the latitude circle labeled 70°N. Then reason: Point B can be read as being near 70°N. At a point 333 kilometers due north of point B, calculating according to about 111 kilometers for each 1° difference in latitude, 333 kilometers is approximately equal to 3° of latitude, so the latitude of this point is 73°N. Since the 70°N where point B is located is the polar day boundary, the midnight solar altitude is 0°, so the solar declination on that date can be obtained as δ=90°-70°=20°N. For this point at 73°N, the maximum solar altitude at noon on that date is: Hmax=90°-|73°-20°|=37°; the minimum solar altitude at midnight is: Hmin=73°+20°-90°=3°. Therefore the range of the solar altitude angle during one day is from 3° to 37°.
